blind.why: 3 Arc shots (spacing copied from the ref) vs trailer_4 @47.0s. B had clean sharp attacks; A was music and VO with one HF transient. The pick is weak: no CS2 trailer has isolated SFX, so every ref clip is contaminated.
Lance vs trailer_1 @45.5s. A was one clear shot; B was continuous music noise with no clear event. The CS2 transient that was visible has centroid ~3.5 kHz. Ours drops below 300 Hz within 20 ms.

Haze pop + hiss vs trailer_4 @16.85s. Ours reads as a smoke (pop, then a steady 2-8 kHz hiss). The ref was narration. pair4/pair5 (Arc, Rail vs trailer_1 @3.77, trailer_2 @1.71) went the same way. All 5 wins come from contaminated refs, so I give them almost no weight.

biggest_gap: Gunfire is dull, tonal and buried under foley/UI. Offline FP renders (node tools/audio_dump.mjs): spectral centroid in the first 100 ms is 145-600 Hz for every tagger (judge 144 Hz, lance 146 Hz, low_ratio 0.93-0.95; >4 kHz energy 0-4%). Level order is inverted: zip/hum/twin/pip fire = -29/-29/-27/-26 LUFS-short, every reload stage hits the limiter (-1.15 dBFS, -17..-21 LUFS) and ui.buy is -15 LUFS. Rail/Arc 'ring' sine partials make a steady 1.83 kHz / 1.38 kHz whistle, +24/+22 dB above the band median over a 12-shot burst (shots/critic-audio/burst_rail.png). CS2 shots are the loudest, brightest event: a broadband 1-8 kHz crack (centroid ~2-3.5 kHz on the transient), non-tonal body, reload foley ~15-20 dB under the shot. Fix: rebuild the crack layer as broadband/saturated noise, cut or detune the ring partials per shot, then rebalance TRIM so fire > hits > foley > UI.
other_gaps: Enemy footsteps are low thuds, not locatable clicks. step.stone TP at 3 m/90° has 3-8 kHz energy 18 dB (near ear) to 36 dB (far ear) below its <300 Hz band. Broadband ILD is only ~2 dB at 90° because energy sits under 300 Hz, so HRTF has almost nothing to work on. CS2 steps are bright scuffs, 1-5 kHz.

Distinctness: judge vs lance band-profile distance is 2.8 dB (pistol and sniper nearly the same spectrum). arc vs scatter 3.1, twin vs zip 3.9, judge vs storm 3.8. *.inspect and *.empty are near-identical across all 12 taggers (same centroid 2389.79 Hz / 563 Hz).

Wiring in the real match (?test=1&seed=1&match=1, input-driven): inspect, slot3 melee, slide, scoreboard and ping produced no sound because no event reached audio. weapon:inspect, weapon:melee, slide, ui:scoreboard and ping are never emitted, so tagger.*.inspect, tagger.tap.fire, move.slide, ui.scoreboard and ui.ping are dead in game. No bot gunfire happened in 2 rounds, so remote fire, occlusion and whiz went unexercised.

Music: the live/menu pads decay to about -45 dB, then retrigger with a +20 dB jump and a broadband click every 2.67 s (HF spikes at 0.06/1.4/2.73/4.06 s in music.live). Whole bed centroid is 127-183 Hz (sub-heavy, no rhythmic identity in 'live').

Positional/reverb: TP renders have almost no reverb (late/early energy 0.001-0.009). Occlusion level 2 costs only ~6.6 dB. 5 m to 25 m is only -6 dB. There's no distant-gunfire character change (CS2 swaps to a distant layer and keeps the crack).

Announcer: a formant buzz with flat pitch; intelligibility can't be verified (no ASR available). 'roundStart' plays twice in round 2: once at buy start (match announce round_start) and again with the horn at live.
hit.tick is -32.6 LUFS, about 10 LU under the shot, so it gets masked during fire. That falls short of the 'loud & clear feedback on every hit' target.
bugs: Double 'Round start' VO per round (announce event round_start at buy + horn() at live). Repro: ?test=1&seed=1&match=1, play to round 2, debug.log shows announce.roundStart before ui.countdown.tick and again after ui.roundstart.horn.
tools/audio_analyze.py crashes (IndexError in rolloff85 searchsorted) on the full 198-sound dump, so metrics.json is never written.
inspect / melee / slide / scoreboard / ping sounds unreachable in game (events not emitted).
Music loop retrigger clicks / amplitude seams in music.live and music.menu every 2.67-2.9 s.
debug.stats shows 10 dropped of 28 plays at round start (8 simultaneous bot draws), so voice stealing is aggressive.
strengths: Large, organised catalogue: 192 sounds + 6 music states render offline with zero failures; clean sharp transients (attack 0.6-4 ms on impacts, ticks and SMG shots)
Round-robin and seed jitter give real variation (spectral corr ~0.94, waveform corr 0.76-0.87 for the same rr with a different seed)
HRTF works in HF (18 dB ILD at 3-8 kHz, 90°). Distance LPF and occlusion LPF are applied
Limiter holds -1.1 dBFS; no clipping in any render or in the live meter
Haze pop + hiss reads well; beacon arm/defuse state machine polled correctly; timer 30/10 s callouts and 10-tick countdown fire on time
